subsystems.name: Elastomeric actuator body
subsystems.role: converts fluid pressure into motion through inflation of internal chambers.

subsystems.name: Reinforcement and strain-limiting layer
subsystems.role: directs bending, contraction, or extension by restricting expansion on one side.

subsystems.name: Fluid power system
subsystems.role: supplies and regulates pressurized air or water to each actuator.

subsystems.name: Sensing and control
subsystems.role: measures actuator state and adjusts pressure to achieve precise motion.

subsystems.name: Array manifold and frame
subsystems.role: distributes fluid to many actuators and holds them in a fixed geometry.

buildSteps.title: Design the array
buildSteps.detail: Decide how many actuators are needed, their layout, and the motion each must produce (bending, twisting, or contracting).

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the actuator bodies
buildSteps.detail: Cast or 3D-print elastomer layers with internal channels, then cure them. Multiple layers are bonded together to form sealed chambers.

buildSteps.title: Add reinforcement
buildSteps.detail: Place inextensible fibers or mesh on one side of each actuator so that inflation causes a controlled bend or contraction rather than simple ballooning.

buildSteps.title: Assemble individual actuators
buildSteps.detail: Bond the layers, insert fluid fittings, and trim to final shape. Each actuator is tested for leaks and stroke.

buildSteps.title: Build the manifold
buildSteps.detail: Connect all actuators to a fluid distribution block that routes pressure from a single supply to each chamber independently.

buildSteps.title: Integrate fluid power
buildSteps.detail: Connect the manifold to a pump or compressor and solenoid valves, using flexible tubing that allows the array to move freely.

buildSteps.title: Add sensors and electronics
buildSteps.detail: Attach pressure and strain sensors, wire them to a microcontroller, and mount the control board.

buildSteps.title: Program control
buildSteps.detail: Write software that maps desired positions or forces to pressure commands, often using empirically tuned models because soft bodies are hard to simulate exactly.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Measure force, speed, and repeatability, then adjust control parameters. Arrays are then integrated into grippers, wearable devices, or other end effectors.

prerequisites.why: soft actuators fatigue and tear after many cycles; longer-lived materials are needed for industrial use.
predicting the motion of a soft structure is difficult, so control is often empirical and slow to tune.
off-the-shelf components work, but further miniaturization would allow denser arrays and faster response.
stretchable strain and pressure sensors are still maturing, limiting real-time feedback in arrays.

pathway.milestone: single soft actuators in commercial grippers for delicate handling
pathway.unlocks: gentle picking of food, produce, and irregular objects in logistics.

pathway.milestone: multi-actuator arrays with integrated sensing for adaptive grasping
pathway.unlocks: robot hands that conform to unknown objects without complex programming.

pathway.milestone: wearable soft exosuits for rehabilitation and assistance
pathway.unlocks: lightweight, comfortable therapy devices that move with the body.

pathway.milestone: fully soft autonomous robots with onboard fluid power and control
pathway.unlocks: safe operation in surgery, search-and-rescue, or exploration where rigid robots fail.
